title: k8s-node-lifecycle-debug-scratchpad
content:
Summary:
- Scratchpad for debugging node provisioning / lifecycle issues observed during recent Dedicated cluster rollouts (us-west-2).
- Symptoms seen: new nodes flapping to NotReady, kubelet crashloops, pods stuck Terminating, helm --wait timeouts on control plane addons.
- Goal: capture commands tried, useful log snippets, hypotheses, and next steps for ops runbook.

Environment/context:
- Cluster: prod-dedicated-usw2 (k8s v1.26)
- Provisioning: Terraform -> ASG + launch template (AMI with containerd 1.6) -> kubeadm bootstrap via user-data systemd service
- CNI: calico v3.25 (DaemonSet)
- Runtime: containerd, cgroup v2 on AMI (custom)

Quick timeline (recent incidents):
- 2024-11-02 03:12 UTC: Autoscaling created 5 new nodes as part of rollout.
- 2024-11-02 03:16 UTC: 3/5 nodes transitioned to NotReady within ~2m.
- 2024-11-02 03:20 UTC: Helm upgrades for kube-proxy/calico timed out waiting for pods to be ready.

Commands tried / outputs (snippets):
- kubectl get nodes -o wide
  NAME                           STATUS     ROLES    AGE    VERSION
  ip-10-0-1-12.ec2.internal      NotReady   <none>   5m     v1.26.3
  ip-10-0-1-13.ec2.internal      Ready      <none>   6m     v1.26.3

- kubectl describe node ip-10-0-1-12.ec2.internal
  Conditions:
    Type             Status  Reason                    Message
    Ready            False   KubeletNotReady           kubelet is posting ready status: false
  Taints:            node.kubernetes.io/unreachable:NoExecute for 5m

- journalctl -u kubelet -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager
  Nov 02 03:13:45 ip-10-0-1-12 systemd[1]: Started kubelet: The Kubernetes Node Agent.
  Nov 02 03:13:47 ip-10-0-1-12 kubelet[1234]: E1102 03:13:47.123456    1234 server.go:123] failed to run Kubelet: failed to register node "ip-10-0-1-12.ec2.internal": node "ip-10-0-1-12.ec2.internal" already exists
  Nov 02 03:13:48 ip-10-0-1-12 kubelet[1234]: E1102 03:13:48.223456    1234 kubelet_node_status.go:96] Error posting node status: Post https://10.0.0.1:6443/api/v1/nodes/ip-10-0-1-12/status: context deadline exceeded

- journalctl -u cloud-init -n 100
  cloud-init[998]: Running /usr/local/bin/kubeadm-join.sh
  cloud-init[998]: ++ kubeadm join --token x.y --discovery-token-ca-cert-hash sha256:abc123 --control-plane
  cloud-init[998]: Error: timed out waiting for the condition

- systemctl status containerd.service
  Active: active (running) since Nov 02 03:13:40
  but containerd logs show repeated errors: failed to create task for container: OCI runtime create failed: runc did not start: exit status 1

- kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide
  NAME                          READY  STATUS             RESTARTS  AGE
  calico-node-abcde             0/1    CrashLoopBackOff    6         4m
  kube-proxy-xxxxx             0/1    CrashLoopBackOff    4         4m

- docker/containerd inspect for calico pod sandbox error:
  "failed to setup network for sandbox ...: failed to discover network config for sandbox"

Hypotheses so far:
1) Node identity / duplicate node names: kubeadm join failed with "node already exists" when re-trying join after partial failure. Could be caused by race when kubelet registers before cloud-init completes creating /etc/kubernetes/kubelet.conf.
2) Cgroup driver mismatch: AMI images moved to cgroup v2; kubelet/containerd config may expect systemd (cgroup v1). Some runc errors suggest OCI runtime issues.
3) Networking not ready: calico containers crash because host networking stack not configured (missing sysctl, missing iptables-nft vs legacy mismatch).
4) Slow kube-apiserver response (context deadline exceeded) during bootstrap causing kubelet to mark node NotReady. API scaling or TLS handshake issues from heavy join burst.
5) ASG lifecycle hook/user-data ordering: kubeadm starts before cloud-init completes additional deps (e.g., install of iptables, modprobe for br_netfilter).

Notes on specific reproducible failures:
- Reproduce (fast): spin up one node from launch-template with user-data and watch systemd services.
- When join fails once, subsequent attempts can hit "node already exists" unless we delete Node from API first: kubectl delete node ip-10-0-1-12.ec2.internal (manual fix)
- Observed that AMI had containerd 1.6.12 + runc 1.1.7; bumped runc locally to 1.1.8 avoided one OCI error (but still saw calico crash).

Temporary mitigations tried:
- Add pre-join sleep in user-data (sleep 60) to allow cloud-init to finish -> decreased frequency but not eliminated.
- Added systemctl restart kubelet after cloud-init completion via ExecStartPost -> improved success rate.
- Drain and cordon problematic nodes until verified: kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data <node>
- For auto-retry: terraform now creates ASG with slower scale-in/out alarms to avoid bursts.

Longer-term changes to try:
- Ensure kubeadm join is only run after cloud-init finalization marker file (e.g., /var/lib/cloud/instance/boot-finished). Use a small wrapper that waits on file + verifies containerd socket exists.
- Make AMI pre-baked with kernel modules (br_netfilter, overlay) and validated containerd/runc combination (baked test script).
- Change kubelet config to be robust for cgroup v2 or pin AMI to cgroup v1 until stable.
- Add mutation webhook or admission check to reject duplicate node register attempts? Probably overkill.

Helpful commands (for next ops run):
- kubectl get nodes -o json | jq '.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, conditions: .status.conditions[-1], taints: .spec.taints}'
- journalctl -u kubelet -o cat -n 500 | sed -n '1,200p' > /tmp/kubelet.log
- sudo ctr -n k8s.io containers list ; sudo crictl pods ; sudo crictl ps -a ; sudo crictl inspectp <sandbox-id>
- sudo modprobe br_netfilter ; sysctl net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables=1
- sudo systemctl restart kubelet && tail -n 200 /var/log/syslog | grep kubelet
- kubectl get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp -A | tail -n 200

Notes from Maya (slack):
- "We saw a similar burst issue in staging; adding a join-wait wrapper that checks 'curl -sf https://10.0.0.1:6443/healthz' before kubeadm join solved most flakes."

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Add healthz probe wait script to user-data and test 10x scale-up in staging.
- [ ] Bake AMI with validated cgroup/runtime combo; create CI test to boot AMI and run quick kubelet/kubeadm smoke test.
- [ ] Investigate API server latency during mass join events; check control plane metrics (etcd CPU, apiserver latencies). Related ticket: INF-342.
- [ ] Update runbook: steps to recover node stuck in NotReady after partial join (delete node, re-run join, or reimage).

Random breadcrumbs / commands I wrote down while on-call:
- to force clean join: kubectl delete nodes ip-10-0-1-12.ec2.internal && sudo kubeadm reset -f && sudo rm -rf /etc/kubernetes/pki/* && kubeadm join ...
- to debug containerd: sudo journalctl -u containerd -n 200 ; sudo ctr t ls ; sudo ctr run --rm --runtime io.containerd.runc.v2 docker.io/library/busybox:1.34 echo hi
- helm upgrade --install calico projectcalico/calico --version v3.25.0 --namespace kube-system --wait --timeout 10m0s  (note: timeout reached when calico-node in CrashLoopBackOff)

Last experimental attempt notes (2024-11-08 15:10 UTC):
- Built a small wrapper script /usr/local/bin/join-if-ready.sh that: waits for /var/lib/cloud/instance/boot-finished, checks containerd socket, curls API server /healthz 5x with backoff, then runs kubeadm join.
- Deployed a test ASG 3-node scale-up in staging using wrapper -> success: 3/3 nodes Ready within 3m.
- Need to run 10-node burst test next (scheduled).

If this doc is useful, copy into Confluence/Runbook and link to INF-342 + PRs.

---
Raw error snippets (grabbed):
- kubeadm join error: "[preflight] Some fatal errors occurred: [ERROR Swap]: running with swap on is not supported. Please disable swap"
- kubelet register: "failed to register node "ip-10-0-1-12.ec2.internal": node "ip-10-0-1-12.ec2.internal" already exists"
- containerd runc: "OCI runtime create failed: runc did not start: exit status 1: [error message about cgroups v2]"
- calico pod: "failed to setup network for sandbox "...": failed to discover network config for sandbox"

Contact: Jordan Kim (Slack @jordan) if you want me to walk through the repro in staging or pair on the AMI bake pipeline.
